t: Turn a pile of case papers into a clear timeline
d: Get a dated, sourced chronology of events from letters, emails and statements, ready for the supervising lawyer to check.
when: When a new matter lands or a file gets messy

steps.h: Check what you are allowed to share
steps.b: Only use an AI tool your firm has approved for client material. If you must use a public one, remove names, addresses and reference numbers first and replace them with labels like [Client] and [Landlord].

steps.h: Gather the documents in date order
steps.b: Collect the key letters, emails and statements for the matter. Copy the text into one document, or attach the files if your approved tool allows it.
Paste this prompt with the material.
steps.p: You are helping a paralegal organise a case file. From the documents below, build a chronology as a table with columns: Date, Event (one plain sentence), Who was involved, Source document and page or paragraph. Use only what the documents say. If a date is unclear, write 'Unclear' and quote the wording. After the table, list: 1) gaps where nothing is recorded, 2) any facts that conflict between documents, 3) questions to ask the client. Do not give legal opinions. Documents: [paste or attach]

steps.h: Check every line against the source
steps.b: Open each source the table points to and confirm the date and wording. AI can misread or invent details, so treat the table as a draft until you have checked it.

steps.h: Hand it to your supervising lawyer
steps.b: Save the checked chronology in the matter folder and send it to the lawyer for review before anyone relies on it.

example:
| 03/02 | Tenant reports leak in writing | [Client], [Landlord] | Email, p1 |
| 17/02 | Landlord replies, no date for repair | [Landlord] | Letter, para 2 |
Gaps: nothing recorded 17/02 to 30/03. Conflict: statement says leak began January, email says February.
tips: Ask for the source column every time. A timeline without sources is hard to check and easy to get wrong.
This is an organising aid, not legal analysis. A qualified lawyer decides what the facts mean.

trigger.detail: Paralegal starts a chronology for a matter

actions.detail: Pull dated events and their sources from the documents
Create a chronology draft in the matter folder
Ask the supervising lawyer to review it

t: Build a numbered exhibit list for trial in an hour
d: A tidy, numbered exhibit schedule in a spreadsheet with short descriptions, dates and page counts, ready for checking and the trial bundle.
when: When preparing a hearing or trial bundle

steps.b: In your document folder, copy the list of file names for the exhibits into a spreadsheet column. Add any notes you already have, such as who produced each one.

steps.h: Ask for a draft exhibit schedule
steps.b: Paste the file list into your firm-approved AI assistant with this prompt. Keep client names out if the tool is not approved for confidential work.
steps.p: Here is a list of exhibit file names and notes for a [type of case] hearing. Create a table I can paste into a spreadsheet with columns: Exhibit number (format [A1, A2...]), Short neutral description (max 12 words), Date of document, Author or source, Number of pages (leave blank if unknown), Party relying on it, Notes. Group by [chronological order / topic / party]. Flag any files that look like duplicates or drafts. Files: [paste list]

steps.b: Paste the table into Excel or Google Sheets, then fill in the page counts and anything marked blank by checking each file yourself.
Rename each file to start with its exhibit number so the folder and the list always match, for example 'A3 Inspection report 2024-05-12'.

Send the schedule to the supervising lawyer to approve the order, descriptions and anything left out before the bundle is finalised. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
A1 | Tenancy agreement | 01/09/2022 | [Agent] | 14 pp | Claimant
A2 | Email reporting damp | 12/01/2024 | [Client] | 1 p | Claimant
A3 | Inspection report | 12/05/2024 | [Surveyor] | 9 pp | Claimant
Flag: 'A2 copy final' looks like a duplicate of A2.
tips: Keep descriptions neutral. Ask the AI to avoid words that argue the case, such as 'proves' or 'admits'.
Check your court's or firm's bundle rules for numbering and indexing, as they vary.

trigger.detail: A document is added to the trial exhibits folder

actions.detail: Suggest a description, date and author for the new file
Add a draft row to the exhibit schedule
Ask the paralegal to check and number it

t: Draft a first-pass affidavit from witness notes
d: Turn interview notes into a clearly numbered draft statement in the witness's own words, ready for lawyer review and the witness to correct.
when: After a witness or client interview

steps.b: Type up or paste your notes from the interview. Replace names and identifying details with labels unless your firm has approved the AI tool for client data.
Paste the notes with this prompt.
steps.p: Turn these interview notes into a first-draft witness statement. Rules: first person, in plain everyday words close to how the witness spoke; short numbered paragraphs; one point per paragraph; in date order; only facts the notes contain, nothing added; mark anything the witness was unsure about with [CHECK]; note where the witness refers to a document with [EXHIBIT?]. Do not include legal conclusions or argument. Leave out any formal heading and declaration, I will add our firm's template. Notes: [paste notes]

steps.h: Drop it into your firm's template
steps.b: Paste the paragraphs into your firm's Word template for affidavits or statements, which has the correct heading, wording and declaration for your court.

steps.h: Review with the lawyer and witness
steps.b: The supervising lawyer must review the draft, and the witness must read and correct every paragraph. It must be their evidence, not the AI's wording. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
1. I have lived at [Address] since March 2021.
2. On or around 12 January 2024 I noticed black mould on the bedroom wall. [CHECK date]
3. I sent an email to the letting agent that evening. [EXHIBIT?]
4. Nobody replied to that email.
tips: Never let a statement go out with the AI's phrasing the witness would not use. Courts expect the witness's own account.
Do not paste confidential client details into a public AI tool unless your firm allows it.

trigger.detail: Paralegal pastes interview notes

actions.detail: Draft numbered statement paragraphs with checks flagged
Create the draft in the firm's statement template
Send to the supervising lawyer for review

t: Send clients clear updates on where their case stands
d: Short, friendly progress emails that explain the latest step and what happens next in plain words, checked by the lawyer before sending.
when: After each step in a matter, or every fortnight

steps.b: Jot down three or four bullet points: what happened, what it means for timing, what you need from the client and the next date. Use labels instead of names if your AI tool is not firm-approved.
Paste your bullets with this prompt.
steps.p: Write a short client update email from a law firm. Audience: [client type, e.g. a private individual with no legal background]. Tone: warm, calm, clear. Structure: 1) one-line summary of where things are, 2) what happened since the last update, 3) what happens next and roughly when, 4) anything we need from them, with a date, 5) who to contact with questions. Under 200 words. Explain any legal terms in brackets. Do not give legal advice or predict the outcome. Notes: [paste bullets]

steps.h: Save it as a reusable template
steps.b: Once you like the shape, save it as an Outlook template or a Gmail template so each update starts from the same clear structure.

Send the draft to the responsible lawyer to check before it goes to the client, especially anything about timing, costs or prospects. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
Subject: Your case: update and next steps
In short: the other side has replied and we are reviewing it.
What's next: we'll send you our thoughts by 14 March.
What we need: a copy of your rent statements by 10 March.
Questions? Call [Name] on [number].
tips: Keep a short 'last update sent' note on the matter so updates stay regular.
Never let AI wording about prospects or outcomes reach a client without a qualified lawyer's check.

trigger.detail: Every other Monday for open matters

actions.detail: Remind the paralegal which clients are due an update
Draft a plain-English update from the matter notes
Save as a draft for lawyer approval

t: Turn your legal research notes into a tidy memo
d: A structured research note listing each source, what it says and its status, with every citation flagged for checking against the original.
when: After a research session, before reporting back

steps.b: Do the research in your usual legal databases and official sources. Copy your notes, the citations you found and the key passages into one document.

steps.h: Ask the AI to organise, not to research
steps.b: Paste your notes with this prompt. You are asking it to structure what you found, not to find new law.
steps.p: Organise my legal research notes into a memo for my supervising lawyer. Use only the sources in my notes and do not add any cases, statutes or quotes of your own. Structure: 1) The question researched, 2) Short answer from the sources (2 to 3 sentences, marked 'for lawyer review'), 3) A table: Source citation exactly as in my notes, What it says (one or two sentences), Pinpoint paragraph or section, Status to check (e.g. still in force, appealed, overruled), 4) Points that conflict or need more research. Notes: [paste notes]

steps.h: Check every citation against the source
steps.b: AI can invent or alter case names, citations and quotes. Open each source in your database and confirm the citation, quote and that it is still good law before the memo goes anywhere.
Give the checked memo to the supervising lawyer. They decide what the research means for the case.

example:
Question: Can a landlord withhold the deposit for normal wear and tear?
Sources table: [Statute s.X] | Sets out deposit rules | s.X(3) | Check: amended 2023?
Conflicts: Note 4 and Note 7 suggest different notice periods. Needs a second look.
tips: If the AI adds a source you did not give it, delete it. Only cite what you have read yourself.
Do not paste client confidential facts into a public AI tool unless your firm allows it. Describe the issue generally instead.

trigger.detail: Paralegal finishes a research session

actions.detail: Structure the notes into a research memo
Save the memo with a citation-check column
Remind the paralegal to verify every citation

t: Send clients a pre-meeting questionnaire that saves time
d: A short online form tailored to the type of matter, so clients arrive with the right facts and papers and the first meeting goes further.
when: When booking a first client meeting

steps.h: Ask for a draft question set
steps.b: Tell your AI assistant the type of matter and paste this prompt. No client details are needed at this stage.
steps.p: I am a paralegal preparing a pre-meeting questionnaire for new clients in [type of matter, e.g. residential lease dispute / will preparation / employment dispute]. Write 10 to 15 clear questions in plain English, grouped under headings (About you, What happened, Key dates, Documents to bring, What you want to achieve). Say for each whether it should be a short answer, long answer, date or yes/no. Add a short friendly intro explaining why we ask and that answers are confidential, and a list of documents to bring. Avoid legal jargon.

steps.b: Create a new form in Microsoft Forms or Google Forms and add the questions with the suggested answer types. Check with your firm that the form tool is approved for client information.
Ask the lawyer who handles these matters to review the questions so nothing important is missed and nothing reads as advice.
Add the form link to your meeting confirmation email template so every new client gets it. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
Key dates: When did you first raise the problem with your landlord? (date)
Documents to bring: tenancy agreement, any emails or letters about the issue, photos, rent statements.
What would a good result look like for you? (long answer)
tips: Keep it under 15 questions. Long forms get abandoned.
Make one version per common matter type and reuse them.

trigger.detail: Client submits the pre-meeting questionnaire

actions.detail: Summarise the answers and list missing information
Save a meeting prep note in the matter folder
Tell the lawyer the prep note is ready

t: Keep every matter's document index up to date each week
d: Incoming correspondence is filed by matter automatically, and a weekly session turns it into an up-to-date index the whole team can trust.
when: Set up once, then every Friday afternoon

steps.h: File emails by matter with rules
steps.b: In Outlook's rules settings, create a rule per busy matter that moves emails containing its reference number into a matter folder. Gmail filters with labels work the same way.

steps.h: Make one index spreadsheet per matter
steps.b: In Excel, create columns: Date, Document type, From, To, Short description, Where saved, Action needed. Save it in the matter folder.
Add a recurring 30-minute Friday event in your calendar called 'Update matter indexes'.

steps.h: Let the AI draft the new rows
steps.b: In the slot, copy the subject lines, dates and senders from the week's matter folder into your firm-approved AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Here is a list of this week's correspondence for matter [reference]. For each item create one row for a document index with columns: Date | Document type (letter, email, court notice, invoice, other) | From | To | Short neutral description (max 12 words) | Action needed (yes/no, and what). Put anything that mentions a deadline or hearing date at the top and mark it DEADLINE. Items: [paste list]

steps.b: Check each row, paste them into the index, and put any deadline into the firm's diary system. Ask the lawyer to confirm any deadline you are unsure about. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
08/03 | Court notice | [Court] | Firm | Hearing listed for 22 April | DEADLINE: yes, diarise
07/03 | Email | [Other side] | Firm | Asks for disclosure list | Yes: draft by 15/03
06/03 | Invoice | [Expert] | Firm | Report fee | Yes: send to accounts
tips: Never rely on AI to calculate court deadlines. Work them out from the rules and have a lawyer confirm them.
Use your firm-approved AI tool only. Subject lines often contain confidential client details.

trigger.detail: Fridays at 3pm

actions.detail: Turn the week's matter emails into index rows and flag deadlines
Add the rows to the matter index
Ask the paralegal to confirm any flagged deadlines

t: Get a first-pass list of risky clauses in any contract
d: A table of clauses worth a closer look, why they may matter for your client and questions to raise, to speed up your own review.
when: Before reviewing a draft contract or lease

steps.h: Use an approved tool or anonymise
steps.b: Use an AI tool your firm has approved for client documents. Otherwise remove party names, prices and identifying details before pasting.

steps.h: Ask for a clause risk table
steps.b: Paste or attach the contract with this prompt.
steps.p: Act as a careful assistant to a lawyer acting for the [buyer / tenant / supplier / customer]. Review the contract below and produce a table with columns: Clause number | What it says in one plain sentence | Why it may matter for my client | Risk level (high, medium, low) | Question or amendment to consider. Focus on: liability and indemnities, termination, payment, renewal, IP, confidentiality, dispute resolution, and anything unusual for a [type of contract]. Quote clause numbers exactly. Then list any standard protections that seem to be missing. This is a first pass for my own review, not advice. Contract: [paste or attach]

steps.h: Check every point in the document
steps.b: Go to each clause it lists and read it yourself. AI can misread wording, miss cross-references or invent clauses, so the table only tells you where to look.

Use the table as a checklist alongside your own review and your firm's precedents. Your professional judgment decides what goes to the client. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
12.3 | Supplier's liability capped at one month's fees | Low cap for a critical service | High | Seek cap of 12 months' fees
18.1 | Auto-renews for 3 years unless 6 months' notice | Easy to miss | Medium | Diarise notice date
Missing: no data protection clause.
tips: Tell it which side you act for. The same clause can be fine for one party and risky for the other.
Never send the AI's table to a client as advice. It is a starting point for your own review.

trigger.detail: A draft contract is saved to the review folder

actions.detail: List clauses by risk level for the acting party
Save a first-pass review table next to the contract
Tell the lawyer the first pass is ready to check

t: Turn your legal advice into a plain-English client letter
d: Rewrite your technical advice note into a clear, warm letter a non-lawyer understands, without changing what you actually advised.
when: After writing an advice note

steps.b: Write your advice as you normally would. The AI only changes the wording for the reader; the advice itself must be yours.
Paste your note, with client names replaced by labels if your AI tool is not firm-approved.
steps.p: Rewrite this lawyer's advice note as a letter to a client with no legal background. Keep every point of advice, recommendation and caveat exactly as given; do not add new advice, options or legal sources. Structure: 1) The short answer in two sentences, 2) Why, in plain words, 3) Your options, as a short list with the pros and cons I gave, 4) What I recommend, 5) What happens next and what I need from you. Explain any legal term in brackets the first time. Reading age around 12. Note: [paste advice]

steps.b: Check the letter against your note to make sure nothing was dropped, softened or overstated, especially caveats and time limits.
Paste the final text into your firm's letter template and send it as you normally would. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
The short answer: you can end the lease early, but only from 1 June and only if your rent is up to date.
Why: your lease has a 'break clause' (a set date when either side can end it)...
What I need from you: confirmation by 20 March that you want to go ahead.
tips: Ask it to keep your caveats word for word if they matter.
Do not paste client confidential details into a public AI tool unless your firm allows it.

trigger.detail: Lawyer pastes a finished advice note

actions.detail: Rewrite the note as a plain-English client letter
Place the draft in the firm letter template
Remind the lawyer to compare it with the original note

t: Draft a witness question outline from the case file
d: A structured outline of topics and questions for examining a witness, linked to the documents, for you to shape into your own plan.
when: When preparing for a hearing or trial

steps.b: Gather the witness's statement, your chronology and the key documents they deal with. Anonymise, or use a firm-approved AI tool.
Paste the material with this prompt.
steps.p: Help me prepare to [examine in chief / cross-examine] a witness in a [type of case]. My client is the [claimant / defendant]. Using only the material below, produce an outline: for each topic, give 1) the point I want to establish, 2) 4 to 6 short, single-fact questions in a logical order ([use leading questions for cross-examination / open questions for examination in chief]), 3) the document and page that supports each point, 4) the likely answer and a risk if the witness disagrees. Flag inconsistencies between the statement and the documents. Material: [paste or attach]

steps.b: Confirm every reference and quote in the original documents. Remove anything the evidence does not support.
Reorder, cut and rewrite the questions to fit your strategy, the court's rules and your own style. The AI outline is a starting point, not a script.

example:
Topic 2: Knowledge of the leak
Point: The witness knew by January.
Q1 You manage the building? Q2 Tenants email you about repairs? Q3 Please look at page 41. That's an email to you dated 12 January? Q4 It mentions water coming through the ceiling?
Risk: may say the email went to spam.
tips: Ask for one fact per question. It keeps the outline tight and easy to adapt.
Any case law or rules the AI mentions must be checked against the source. AI can invent cases.

trigger.detail: Lawyer starts witness preparation

actions.detail: Create a topic and question outline with document links
Save the outline to the trial preparation folder

t: Stress-test your argument before a hearing
d: Hear the strongest points the other side is likely to make, the weak spots in your own case and questions a judge may ask, so nothing surprises you.
when: A few days before a hearing or meeting

steps.b: Write a one-page summary of the facts, the issues and your main arguments. Leave out names and anything confidential unless your AI tool is firm-approved.

steps.h: Ask it to argue the other side
steps.b: Paste the summary with this prompt.
steps.p: Here is a summary of my argument in a [type of case] where I act for the [party]. Play the role of experienced opposing counsel. 1) Give the 5 strongest counter-arguments, most dangerous first. 2) For each, say which fact or gap in my case it exploits. 3) List 5 questions a judge might ask me. 4) Suggest what further evidence or points would answer each weakness. Base this on the facts given. If you mention any case or statute, label it 'unverified' so I can check it. Summary: [paste]

steps.b: AI can invent case names and citations that look real. Treat every authority it mentions as unverified until you have read it in a proper legal source.
Add answers to the strongest points to your notes, and discuss any serious weaknesses with colleagues or the client as you normally would.

example:
1. Notice was never given in writing, so the clause wasn't triggered. (Exploits: no letter on file.)
2. Your client kept paying rent, which suggests they accepted the state of the property.
Judge may ask: 'Why did your client wait four months to complain?'
tips: Ask for a second round: 'Now reply to each counter-argument as if you were me' to test your answers.
Use it for preparation only. Your professional judgment decides the strategy.

trigger.detail: Three days before a hearing in the calendar

actions.detail: Remind the lawyer to run a stress-test
List counter-arguments and likely judge questions

t: Plan a settlement negotiation with clear fall-back positions
d: A one-page negotiation plan with your aims, walk-away point, likely offers from the other side and well-worded responses, agreed with the client.
when: Before a settlement meeting or mediation

steps.b: Note the issues in dispute, the client's instructions, what they must have and what they can trade. Keep identifying details out unless your tool is firm-approved.
Paste your notes with this prompt.
steps.p: Help me plan a settlement negotiation in a [type of dispute]. I act for the [party]. Using my notes, produce a one-page plan: 1) Our goals ranked, 2) Our opening position and the reasoning to give, 3) Concessions we could trade, in the order we would offer them, 4) Walk-away point as instructed, 5) The other side's likely interests and three offers they may make, 6) A calm, professional response to each offer, 7) Non-money terms to consider (timing, confidentiality, apology, references). Do not set numbers I have not given you. Notes: [paste]

steps.b: Go through the plan with the client and get clear instructions on the walk-away point and any concessions. The decisions are theirs and yours, not the AI's.

steps.h: Keep it handy on the day
steps.b: Save a short version in your notes app to glance at during breaks. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
Goals: 1) Deposit returned in full 2) Costs contribution 3) Neutral reference.
Trade first: drop the claim for interest.
Likely offer: half the deposit. Reply: 'We hear that, but the inventory shows no damage beyond normal wear. We'd need the full deposit to settle today.'
tips: Ask it to suggest the other side's interests, not just their positions. It helps find deals.
Settlement figures and terms must come from the client's instructions and your professional judgment.

trigger.detail: A settlement meeting is booked

actions.detail: Draft a one-page negotiation plan from the notes
Save the plan in the matter folder
Remind the lawyer to confirm instructions with the client

t: Turn a new regulation into a briefing for business clients
d: A short, plain-English client alert on what a new rule changes, who it affects and what to do next, checked by you before it goes out.
when: When a new law, rule or guidance is published

steps.b: Download the regulation or guidance from the official government or regulator website. Work from that, not from news reports.
Attach or paste the official text with this prompt.
steps.p: Using only the official text below, draft a client briefing for [type of business, e.g. small landlords / online retailers]. Sections: 1) What has changed, in three sentences, 2) Who it applies to and who it doesn't, 3) Key dates, 4) What businesses should do now, as a checklist, 5) Common questions with short answers. Quote the section or paragraph number for every point. Plain English, under 600 words. Do not mention any case law. Add a line saying this is general information, not legal advice. Text: [paste or attach]

steps.h: Check every point against the text
steps.b: Read the source alongside the draft and confirm each section reference, date and obligation. Fix anything that overstates or simplifies too far.

Put the checked briefing into your firm's template, send it to clients through Mailchimp or your usual mailing tool, and share a short summary on LinkedIn if your firm does that. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law. Don't paste client confidential details into a public AI tool unless your firm allows it.

example:
What has changed: from 1 October, landlords must give tenants an energy rating before any viewing (s.4).
Who it applies to: all residential lettings; holiday lets are excluded (s.2(3)).
Do now: check your adverts, update your viewing pack...
This is general information, not legal advice.
tips: Ask it for a list of questions it couldn't answer from the text. Those are often where clients need you.
Keep the 'not legal advice' line and your firm's usual disclaimer on every briefing.

trigger.detail: Lawyer adds a new official text to the briefings folder

actions.detail: Draft a sectioned client briefing with references
Create the briefing in the firm template
Ask the lawyer to check it before sending

t: Write a file note after every client call, automatically
d: Each client call becomes a draft attendance note with advice given, instructions received and tasks, waiting for you to check and file.
when: After every recorded client call

steps.b: Confirm your firm allows recording and AI notes for client calls, and always tell the client and get their agreement before recording.
If your plan includes it, switch on Teams Copilot recap or Zoom AI Companion for client calls. If not, turn on the transcript and save it after the call.

steps.h: Turn the transcript into a file note
steps.b: Paste the recap or transcript into your firm-approved AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Turn this call transcript into a law firm attendance note. Format: Matter: [reference] | Date and time | Attendees | Duration. Then sections: 1) Purpose of call, 2) Facts the client told us, 3) Advice given, quoting exactly what was said where it matters, 4) Instructions received, 5) Tasks with owner and due date, 6) Anything the client was unsure about. Use only what is in the transcript. Mark unclear parts [UNCLEAR]. Transcript: [paste]

steps.b: Read the note against your memory and the transcript. Pay closest attention to the advice and instructions sections, which you are professionally responsible for.

steps.h: File it and add the tasks
steps.b: Save the note to the matter in your case management system or folder, and add the tasks to your to-do list or the team's board. If the AI mentions any case or law, check it against the original source, as AI can invent case law.

example:
Purpose: discuss landlord's offer.
Advice given: 'I think the offer is low given the inspection report, but it is your decision.'
Instructions: reject the offer; counter at full deposit.
Tasks: [Lawyer] to write to other side by 14/03. [Client] to send photos by 12/03.
tips: Never file a note you haven't checked. An attendance note is a professional record.
Delete recordings and transcripts in line with your firm's retention policy once the note is filed.

trigger.detail: A client call ends

actions.detail: Draft an attendance note from the transcript
Save the draft note to the matter folder
Add the agreed tasks to the to-do list
Ask the lawyer to check and approve the note

t: Write a property listing that gets more viewings
d: A clear, appealing property description, key features list and short social post from your photos and notes, written in minutes.
when: After every valuation or new instruction

steps.h: Note the facts on the visit
steps.b: In your notes app, record room sizes, the best features, local selling points and anything the seller loves about the home. Snap the main rooms on your phone.
Open your AI assistant, attach a few photos and paste this prompt with your notes.
steps.p: Write a property listing for a [property type] for [sale / rent] at [asking price]. Ideal buyer: [e.g. first-time buyers, growing families, downsizers]. Using my notes and photos, give me: 1) A headline of max 10 words, 2) A 120-word description that leads with the best feature, 3) 8 bullet key features, 4) A room-by-room section using my measurements, 5) A 40-word social post. Warm, honest, no clichés like 'deceptively spacious' or 'must be seen'. Only state facts from my notes; if something is unclear, leave a [CHECK]. Notes: [paste notes]

steps.b: Check every measurement, feature and claim against your notes and the seller. Listings must be accurate, so remove anything you can't back up.
Paste the text into your property portal and website listings, and use the social post for your agency's pages.

example:
Headline: Sunny three-bed with a south-facing garden
Description: Morning light fills the kitchen-diner of this three-bedroom semi, set on a quiet street a short walk from the station...
Key features: south-facing garden, new boiler 2023, driveway for two cars...
tips: Don't describe who 'should' live there in ways that exclude people, such as 'perfect for young professionals only'. Describe the home, not the buyer.
Keep the seller's details and address number out of the prompt if you don't need them.

trigger.detail: Agent adds valuation notes and photos

actions.detail: Write a headline, description, features and social post
Save the listing draft for checking

t: Shortlist homes that fit each buyer's brief
d: Buyers fill in a short form, and you get a ranked shortlist from your current stock with a friendly email explaining why each home fits.
when: Whenever a new buyer registers

steps.b: In Google Forms, ask for budget, mortgage position, must-haves, nice-to-haves, areas, timing and anything they can't live with. Responses land in a Google Sheet.
In another tab, list your available properties with price, area, bedrooms, outside space, parking, chain status and listing link.
Copy the buyer's answers and your stock list into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Here is a buyer's brief and my current list of available properties. Rank the 5 best matches. For each: property, price, how well it matches (strong / partial), which must-haves it meets, which it misses, and one line on why it's worth a look. Exclude anything over [budget + 5%] or missing a must-have, unless nothing else fits. Then write a short, friendly email to the buyer introducing the top 3 with links and inviting them to book viewings. Brief: [paste] Stock: [paste]

steps.b: Check the matches make sense, edit the email so it sounds like you, and send it from Gmail.

example:
1. 14 Elm Row, 3 bed, asking within budget: strong match (garden, parking, near schools). Misses: second bathroom.
2. Flat 2, Mill House: partial (no garden, but balcony and station 5 min).
Email: 'Hi Sam, I've picked three homes I think you'll like...'
tips: Ask buyers about features, not about who they are. Matching on things like family status or background can be discriminatory.
Only paste the details you need. Leave out buyers' financial documents.

trigger.detail: A buyer submits the brief form

actions.detail: Rank current stock against the buyer's brief
Draft an introduction email with the top 3 homes
Record the shortlist against the buyer

t: Back up your asking price with recent local sales
d: A clear, one-page pricing case comparing the home with recent nearby sales, so sellers understand why you're recommending the price.
when: Before a valuation appointment

steps.b: From the sold prices data you normally use, list 4 to 6 similar nearby homes sold recently with price, date, size, bedrooms, condition and anything notable.
Paste the comparables and the subject property's details with this prompt.
steps.p: I'm an estate agent preparing for a valuation. Subject property: [details]. Recent comparable sales: [paste table]. Produce: 1) A table comparing each sale with the subject property, noting what's better, worse or similar (size, condition, garden, parking, location), 2) A short explanation of a sensible price range based only on these sales, showing your reasoning, 3) Three points to explain to the seller in plain words, 4) Questions the seller is likely to ask and short answers. Do not invent sales or prices. Flag where the data is thin.

steps.b: Check the reasoning against your local knowledge and the current market. The final valuation is your professional view, not the AI's.
Paste the comparison table and key points into a short Google Doc to share at the appointment.

example:
22 Oak Rd sold 4 months ago: same size, but needs a new kitchen (subject is better).
9 Ash Cl sold 2 months ago: larger garden, same condition (subject slightly weaker).
Suggested range: between the two, nearer 22 Oak Rd plus kitchen premium. Data thin: only 2 sales in the last 3 months.
tips: Always give the AI the real sold data. Never ask it to guess local prices; it will make them up.
Leave the seller's name out. The property details are enough.

trigger.detail: A valuation appointment is booked

actions.detail: Remind the agent to gather comparables
Build a comparison table and pricing explanation
Create a one-page seller handout

t: Explain an offer to your seller clearly and fairly
d: A clear summary of each offer with the buyer's position, conditions and timing, so your seller can compare them and decide.
when: Whenever an offer comes in

steps.b: Write down the amount, the buyer's position (chain, mortgage agreed in principle, cash), conditions, preferred timing and anything they said about the home.
Paste the details with this prompt. Use first names or 'Buyer A' rather than full details.
steps.p: I'm an estate agent presenting offers to a seller. Asking price: [price]. Offers: [paste details for each]. Write a short email to the seller that: 1) Lists each offer in a simple table (amount, difference from asking, buyer position, conditions, timing), 2) Explains in neutral plain words the strengths and risks of each, 3) Sets out the seller's options (accept, counter, wait), 4) Asks for their decision by [time]. Be balanced and factual; do not pressure the seller or recommend a choice.

steps.h: Add your view in your own words
steps.b: If you give a recommendation, write it yourself after checking it fits your duties to the seller. Then send the email and follow up with a call.

example:
Offer A: 5% under asking, first-time buyer, mortgage agreed in principle, no chain, wants to complete in 8 weeks.
Offer B: 2% under asking, has a home to sell, not yet on the market.
Options: accept A, counter A, or wait for B to sell.
tips: Pass on every offer as your rules require, even ones you think are low.
Keep buyers' financial details out of the AI tool; a short description of their position is enough.

trigger.detail: An email containing a new offer arrives

actions.detail: Pull out amount, position, conditions and timing
Draft a neutral offer summary for the seller

t: Give sellers a room-by-room checklist before photos and viewings
d: A friendly, prioritised to-do list for each room, from quick tidies to small fixes, so the home looks its best for photos and viewings.
when: After the valuation, before the photographer visits

steps.b: Take one wide photo of each main room and the outside, as the room looks today.
Attach the photos to your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: These photos are of a home about to go on the market. For each room, give a short, friendly checklist for the seller, sorted into: 1) Free and under 15 minutes (declutter, tidy, open curtains), 2) Small costs (bulbs, a plant, touch-up paint), 3) Bigger jobs only worth doing if [budget/time allows]. Max 5 items per room. Explain in one line why the top item matters for buyers. Be kind; the seller lives here. Rooms in photos: [list]

steps.h: Check it and make it personal
steps.b: Remove anything that doesn't suit the home or the seller's budget, and add your own local knowledge of what buyers look for.
Send the checklist by email or WhatsApp with the photography date, and offer to answer questions.

example:
Kitchen: 1) Clear worktops except the kettle (free, 10 min). 2) Replace the two dead spotlights (small cost). Why: buyers judge kitchens first.
Garden: 1) Mow and sweep the patio. 2) Two potted plants by the door.
tips: Ask the seller's permission before you send photos of their home to an AI tool, and avoid photos showing family pictures or post.
Keep a copy as a template for similar homes.

trigger.detail: Agent uploads room photos after a valuation

actions.detail: Write a room-by-room prep checklist
Send the checklist to the seller

t: Keep every sale moving from offer to completion
d: A simple sales progression tracker plus weekly, polite chasing emails to solicitors, lenders and surveyors so no sale stalls quietly.
when: Set up once, then every Monday morning

steps.b: In Google Sheets, make one row per agreed sale with columns for each milestone: memorandum sent, searches ordered, survey done, mortgage offer, enquiries raised, enquiries answered, exchange, completion, plus 'last update' and 'who we're waiting on'.
Create a recurring Monday 30-minute event called 'Sales progression' so the chase never slips.

steps.h: Let the AI spot stuck sales and draft chasers
steps.b: Copy the sheet into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Here is my sales progression tracker. Today is [date]. 1) List sales where nothing has changed for over [10] days, oldest first, and say what is holding each one up. 2) For each stuck step, draft a short, polite chasing email to the right person (buyer's solicitor, seller's solicitor, lender, surveyor), naming the property and the exact item needed. 3) Write a two-line update for each seller and buyer. Tracker: [paste]

steps.b: Check the drafts, add names and send from Gmail. Update the 'last update' column as replies arrive.

example:
Stuck: 14 Elm Row, 16 days since enquiries were raised. Waiting on seller's solicitor.
Chaser: 'Hi [Name], I'm checking in on 14 Elm Row. Could you let me know when replies to the buyer's enquiries are likely? The buyer is keen to exchange this month.'
tips: Keep personal and financial details out of the sheet you paste. Property name and milestone dates are enough.
Colour rows red in the sheet when 'days since update' passes 10 so stuck sales stand out.

trigger.detail: Mondays at 9am

actions.detail: Find sales with no progress for over 10 days
Draft polite chasers to the right people
Send the agent a list of stuck sales

t: Keep in touch with past buyers and sellers all year
d: A light, personal touch with past clients each quarter and on their home anniversary, so they think of you when they or friends move.
when: Set up once, then quarterly and on anniversaries

steps.h: List past clients who agreed to hear from you
steps.b: In Google Sheets, list past clients who gave permission to be contacted, with first name, area, move date and anything useful they shared (such as a renovation plan).
Add a yearly Google Calendar event on each move-in date, so you get a nudge to send a personal note.
Each quarter, paste your notes about the local market into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Write a short, friendly quarterly email to past clients of a local estate agent in [area]. Include: 1) A two-sentence local market update from my notes (no figures I haven't given you), 2) One practical home tip for the season, 3) One local event or new opening, 4) A gentle line saying I'm happy to give a free valuation or recommend a tradesperson. Under 200 words, warm, no hard sell. Notes: [paste notes]

steps.b: Paste the email into a Mailchimp campaign for your past-client audience and schedule it. Mailchimp handles unsubscribes for you.
When an anniversary reminder pops up, ask the AI for a three-line note using the client's first name and one detail, then edit it and send it yourself.

example:
Subject: Spring on Riverside: a quick update
Homes near the park are still selling quickly, and we've seen more first-time buyers this spring.
Seasonal tip: clear gutters before the April showers.
New: the Saturday market is back on the green.
tips: Only email people who agreed to it, and make it easy to unsubscribe. Marketing email rules apply.
Personal notes beat newsletters. Keep the anniversary note short and genuine.

trigger.detail: First Monday of each quarter, plus each client's move-in date

actions.detail: Draft the quarterly update or anniversary note
Prepare the Mailchimp campaign or personal email
Ask the agent to review before sending

t: Handle a tenant complaint fairly using your house rules
d: A calm, fair reply to a tenant or resident complaint that follows your own rules and process, with a clear log entry and next steps.
when: Whenever a complaint or neighbour dispute comes in

steps.h: Collect the complaint and your rules
steps.b: Copy the complaint and the relevant part of your tenancy terms, house rules or complaints policy. Remove names and flat numbers if your AI tool is not approved for this.
Paste both with this prompt.
steps.p: I'm a property manager. Here is a complaint from a [tenant / resident] and the relevant rules. 1) Summarise the complaint in two sentences. 2) Say which rules apply and how, quoting them. 3) List facts I need to check before deciding. 4) Draft a calm, respectful reply that acknowledges the issue, explains what we will do and by when, and how they can escalate under our complaints process. Do not admit fault or promise anything the rules don't support. Under 200 words. Complaint: [paste] Rules: [paste]

steps.b: Check the facts the AI listed before you send anything. If the complaint involves discrimination, harassment, safety or a legal dispute, speak to your manager or legal adviser first.
Send the reply, then record the complaint, your response and the follow-up date in your complaints log.

example:
Summary: Flat [3] reports noise from Flat [5] after 11pm on several weekdays.
Rule: House rule 7, 'no noise likely to disturb neighbours between 11pm and 7am'.
Check: any earlier reports? Reply: 'Thank you for letting us know. We'll write to the resident this week...'
tips: Treat both sides the same. Ask the AI to check your draft for tone if you're dealing with a repeat complainer.
Keep residents' personal details out of public AI tools.

trigger.detail: An email arrives in the complaints inbox

actions.detail: Summarise the complaint and match it to the rules
Draft a fair reply for the manager to check
Add the complaint to the complaints log

t: Write a clear scope of works contractors can price
d: A tidy job specification from your notes and photos, so every contractor quotes for the same work and quotes are easy to compare.
when: Before asking for quotes on repairs or improvements

steps.b: Take clear photos of the area and jot down what's wrong, rough measurements, access arrangements and any constraints such as working hours.

steps.h: Ask for a scope of works
steps.b: Attach the photos and paste your notes with this prompt.
steps.p: Write a scope of works for contractors to quote against. Property type: [e.g. block of 12 flats]. Job: [short description]. Use my notes and photos. Sections: 1) Background, 2) Work required, as numbered items, 3) Materials or standards required [if known], 4) Access, working hours and resident considerations, 5) Health and safety and waste removal, 6) What the quote must include (itemised costs, timescale, insurance details, guarantee), 7) Questions contractors should answer. Mark anything I need to confirm with [CHECK]. Notes: [paste]

steps.b: Fill in the [CHECK] items. For structural, gas, electrical or fire safety work, have a qualified surveyor or engineer review the scope.

steps.h: Send the same pack to every contractor
steps.b: Save it as a Word document and send it with the photos to each contractor, with a return date for quotes.

example:
Work required: 1) Remove and dispose of damaged guttering on the rear elevation (approx. 14 m). 2) Supply and fit new uPVC guttering and two downpipes. 3) Clear the gully at the base of the rear downpipe.
Access: scaffold tower needed; residents' car park must stay open.
tips: The more precise the scope, the easier it is to compare quotes fairly afterwards.
Ask for proof of insurance and any required certificates in every quote.

trigger.detail: Manager adds notes and photos for a new job

actions.detail: Write a numbered scope of works
Save the scope as a document ready to send

t: Check your rental adverts are fair to everyone
d: Get your rental adverts checked for wording that could put people off or exclude them unfairly, with fairer alternatives ready to use.
when: Before any rental advert goes live

steps.b: Copy the advert text, including any 'requirements' section.
Paste it into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Review this rental advert for wording that could discriminate against, or put off, people because of characteristics protected by law where I am ([country or state]), such as race, religion, sex, disability, age, family status or receiving benefits. For each issue: quote the wording, explain in one line why it could be a problem, and suggest a fairer alternative that describes the property or the objective requirement instead. Then check the advert is clear on rent, deposit, fees and accessibility features. Advert: [paste]

steps.b: The AI can miss local rules or flag things that are fine. If you're unsure, check with your compliance team or a legal adviser before publishing.
Keep the corrected advert as a template so future adverts start fair.

example:
Issue: 'Ideal for young professionals' could put off older applicants. Try: 'Close to the station and city centre.'
Issue: 'No children' may be unlawful where you are. Try describing the property, e.g. 'One-bedroom flat, suits one or two people.'
tips: Describe the home and the objective requirements, such as rent and references, not the kind of person you want.
This is a checking aid, not legal advice. Rules differ by country and state.

trigger.detail: A new advert draft is saved to the adverts folder

actions.detail: Flag wording that may be unfair or exclusionary
Send the flags to the manager before publishing

t: Turn inspection photos into a tidy condition report
d: Walk round with your phone, then get a room-by-room condition report with issues ranked by urgency and a maintenance to-do list.
when: After every routine inspection

steps.h: Photograph and talk as you go
steps.b: In each room or area, take photos and record a short voice note of what you see. Avoid photographing tenants, their post or personal papers.
Use your phone's voice note transcription, or describe each area in a few typed lines in your notes app.
Attach the photos and paste your notes into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Create a property inspection report from my notes and photos. Property: [address label or reference], date: [date]. For each area: condition (good / fair / poor), what I observed, and any issue. Then a table of issues: Issue | Location | Urgency (urgent within 24 hours / within 2 weeks / next planned maintenance) | Suggested action | Who should do it (tenant, contractor, owner). Only report what is in my notes or clearly visible; mark anything uncertain [CHECK]. Notes: [paste]

steps.b: Check the report against your photos, then save it in Google Docs in the property's folder with the photos.
Raise jobs for urgent items straight away, and send the owner a short summary.

example:
Bathroom: fair. Sealant around bath discoloured and lifting.
Issue table: Damp patch on bedroom ceiling | Bedroom 2 | Within 2 weeks | Investigate roof or flat above | Contractor
Smoke alarm not tested | Hall | Urgent | Test and replace battery | Manager
tips: Safety issues like gas smells, exposed wiring or failed alarms need action at once, not a report.
Use the same format every time so you can compare inspections over the years.

trigger.detail: Inspection photos and notes are added to the property folder

actions.detail: Write a room-by-room condition report
Save the report with the photos
Add urgent issues to the maintenance list

t: Prepare a residents' board meeting pack in an hour
d: A clear agenda, short summary papers and decisions needed for a residents' association or board meeting, from your notes and reports.
when: A week before each board or residents' meeting

steps.b: Collect the last minutes, open actions, budget figures, repair updates and any disputes or issues to raise. Leave out residents' names where they're not needed.
Paste the material with this prompt.
steps.p: I manage a [building / estate] and need a board meeting pack. From my notes, create: 1) A timed agenda (max 90 minutes), 2) For each item a half-page paper: background, current position, options, and the decision needed from the board, 3) An updated action log from the last minutes, showing done, in progress or overdue, 4) A one-paragraph cover note for board members. Use only my figures. Be neutral on disputes between residents. Notes: [paste]

steps.b: Check every number against your accounts. For legal disputes or environmental issues, ask your legal or specialist adviser to review the paper before it's circulated.
Format the pack in your template and send it to board members with enough time to read it.

example:
Item 3: Roof repairs (15 min)
Background: survey found worn flashing on the north side.
Options: patch repair now, or full replacement in the next financial year.
Decision needed: approve patch repair quote within the reserve fund limit.
tips: Put 'decision needed' in bold on every paper. Meetings go faster when everyone knows what they're deciding.
Minutes and action logs from this pack make next month's pack quicker.

trigger.detail: One week before a board meeting

actions.detail: Remind the manager to gather meeting inputs
Draft the agenda, papers and action log
Create the meeting pack

t: Build a planned maintenance calendar for every building
d: A year-round maintenance plan for each property in a spreadsheet, with reminders in your calendar so checks and services never slip.
when: Once a year, then follow the reminders

steps.b: Note the main systems and features for each property: boilers, lifts, fire alarms, emergency lighting, gutters, roofs, gardens, communal areas.
Paste the list with this prompt.
steps.p: I manage [number] properties. For each, here are the main systems and features: [paste]. Create a planned maintenance schedule as a table: Property | Item | Task | How often | Suggested month | Who usually does it (contractor type) | Notes. Spread the work across the year so no month is overloaded. Mark tasks that are often legal or insurance requirements with [CHECK REQUIREMENT] so I confirm the rules that apply where I am ([country or state]).

steps.b: Check the [CHECK REQUIREMENT] items against official guidance, your insurer and any compliance adviser, and adjust how often they happen.

steps.h: Put it in a sheet and calendar
steps.b: Paste the table into Google Sheets with a 'last done' column. Then add each task to Google Calendar as a recurring event with a two-week reminder.

example:
Block A | Fire alarm | Weekly test | Weekly | All year | Caretaker | Log in fire book [CHECK REQUIREMENT]
Block A | Gutters | Clear and inspect | Twice yearly | Apr, Nov | Roofing contractor
Block B | Lift | Service | Every 6 months | Mar, Sep | Lift engineer
tips: Add a 'last done' date and a link to each certificate so you can show evidence quickly if asked.
Review the plan each year and after any major repair.

trigger.detail: Two weeks before each planned task

actions.detail: Remind the manager to book the contractor
Add the confirmed visit to the calendar
Update 'last done' once complete

t: Log and prioritise every repair request from one form
d: Tenants report repairs through one form; each request is logged, sorted by urgency and answered with a clear acknowledgement.
when: Set up once, then every time a repair is reported

steps.b: In Google Forms, ask for property and flat reference, contact details, what's wrong, where, since when, whether it's getting worse, photos, and access times. Add a clear line telling people to phone your emergency number for gas leaks, floods or no heating.
Link the form to a Google Sheet and add columns for urgency, contractor, status and date fixed.
Once or twice a day, copy new rows into your AI assistant with this prompt. Leave out contact details.
steps.p: Here are new repair requests from tenants. For each: 1) Urgency: Emergency (same day), Urgent (within 3 working days), Routine (within [x] weeks), using our policy: [paste your response times], 2) Likely trade needed, 3) A friendly two-sentence acknowledgement email to the tenant saying what happens next and when. If anything sounds like a safety risk, put it first and mark SAFETY. Requests: [paste]

steps.b: Paste the urgency and trade into the sheet, and send the acknowledgements from Gmail using saved templates for each urgency level.
Always read safety and emergency items yourself and act on them straight away. Don't rely on the AI's triage alone.

example:
SAFETY | Flat [4] | Water coming through ceiling light | Emergency, electrician and plumber
Flat [9] | Kitchen tap dripping | Routine, plumber
Ack: 'Thanks for reporting the dripping tap. We've logged it and a plumber will contact you within 10 working days to arrange a visit.'
tips: Set the form to show your emergency phone number at the top. A form is not the right channel for emergencies.
Store tenant contact details only in the sheet, not in the AI chat.

trigger.detail: A tenant submits a repair request

actions.detail: Set urgency and likely trade using the repairs policy
Record urgency and status in the repairs log
Draft an acknowledgement to the tenant
Alert the manager immediately for safety items
